note: One private cellar. Quantities are often one. Prices are quoted privately.

wines.name: Adrianna Vineyard, Mundus Bacillus Terrae
wines.story: A single block of the Adrianna Vineyard at 1,450 metres, on limestone, named for the soil bacteria that make it. Catena’s grand cru, and a perfect score in 2021.

wines.name: Bodega Chacra ‘32’
wines.story: Pinot Noir from vines planted in 1932, bought and revived by Piero Incisa della Rocchetta of the Sassicaia family. The 2018 was named Wine of the Year by James Suckling.

wines.name: Bodega La Rural, Felipe Rutini
wines.story: Founded in 1885 by Felipe Rutini, La Rural is the oldest working winery in Mendoza. Its top cuvée from the 1980s and 1990s is almost impossible to find outside Argentina.

wines.name: Bodega López Montchenot
wines.story: Montchenot is the historic top wine of one of Mendoza’s oldest family bodegas, aged for years before release. Two magnums from 1975.

wines.name: Catena Zapata Estiba Reservada
wines.story: The first vintage was 1990, made from the oldest Cabernet at La Pirámide and released only when Nicolás Catena judged it ready. It is the wine that told the world Argentina could age.

wines.name: Cobos Malbec Marchiori Estate
wines.story: Paul Hobbs’ Argentine project, from old Malbec vines on the Marchiori family estate. The 2011 earned a perfect score, and the magnums came directly from the bodega.

wines.name: Uni del Bonnesant ‘312’, Perse
wines.story: From a single high-altitude parcel in Gualtallary, made by David Bonomi and Edy del Pópolo. Tim Atkin named it Wine of the Year, twice.

wines.name: Weinert Malbec Estrella
wines.story: Cavas de Weinert age their wines in old French oak for years before release, and Estrella is made only in exceptional vintages. This is the first edition, from 1977.

wines.name: Château Haut-Brion
wines.story: The oldest of the first growths, already famous in London in the 1660s. The 1959 is a legendary vintage that has earned a perfect score, and at over sixty years it still carries the estate’s signature of warm bricks and tobacco.

wines.name: Château Latour
wines.story: The 1961 vintage is the yardstick every other Bordeaux year is measured against, and Latour made the wine of the vintage. This bottle comes from the Berry Bros. & Rudd Family Reserves, one of the finest private cellars in London.

wines.name: Château Mouton Rothschild
wines.story: Every vintage since 1945 carries a label by a different artist. The 1993 drawing by Balthus was refused in the United States, so American bottles shipped with a blank label. These carry the drawing.

holdings.condition: good levels and lovely Balthus labels

wines.name: Le Pin
wines.story: A garden of barely two hectares bought by the Thienpont family in 1979, fermented in a cellar under a modest house. Production rarely passes a few hundred cases, which is why Le Pin became the first cult wine of Bordeaux.

wines.name: Liber Pater
wines.story: Loïc Pasquet replanted forgotten pre-phylloxera varieties on their own roots, at the densities of the 19th century. A few hundred bottles a year, and by some distance the most expensive young wine in Bordeaux.

wines.name: Pétrus
wines.origin: Pomerol, right bank of the Dordogne
wines.story: Eleven hectares of blue clay on the Pomerol plateau, farmed by the Moueix family and made almost entirely from Merlot. Pétrus never had a château to speak of; it had the soil, and the soil made it the most sought-after wine in Bordeaux.

wines.name: Bourgogne Blanc, Domaine Leroy
wines.story: The regional white from the same hands as the Musigny, farmed biodynamically to yields that would make most growers weep. The 2016 was a tiny, frost-struck crop.

wines.name: Chablis Les Clos, Vincent Dauvissat
wines.story: The greatest of the Chablis grands crus, from a grower who still ploughs by horse in places and bottles with a minimum of intervention. Les Clos is stony, saline and long-lived.

wines.name: Clos de la Roche, Jacky Truchot
wines.story: Jacky Truchot retired in 2005 and sold his vines, and his pale, whole-cluster wines went from local secret to obsession. The grand cru Clos de la Roche was his largest holding, which still meant only a few barrels.

wines.name: La Tâche
wines.story: Six hectares, one owner, and a wine that is often the most exotic in the domaine’s range: spice, rose and iron. Older bottles were labelled with the level at the neck, as the 1992 is here.

wines.name: Musigny, Domaine Leroy
wines.story: Lalou Bize-Leroy farms 0.27 hectares of Musigny biodynamically and bottles a few hundred bottles in a good year. It has become the most expensive wine in the world at auction, and almost never leaves the cellars it enters.

wines.name: Romanée-Conti
wines.story: A monopole of 1.8 hectares that yields around five thousand bottles a year, sold only as part of a mixed case. Nothing in Burgundy is more difficult to obtain, or more quietly resold.

wines.name: Vosne-Romanée, Henri Jayer
wines.story: Henri Jayer made wine from 1951 until 2001 and taught a generation of Burgundy to destem and to wait. His village Vosne-Romanée is the humblest bottle he signed, and one of the rarest things a collector can open.

wines.name: Screaming Eagle
wines.story: Around five hundred cases a year, sold only through a mailing list with a decade-long wait. The 2019 earned a perfect score.

wines.name: Bollinger Vieilles Vignes Françaises
wines.story: Blanc de noirs from two tiny plots of ungrafted vines that survived phylloxera, worked by hand and by hoe. Around three thousand bottles in a good year.

wines.name: Dom Pérignon
wines.story: The 1960s vintages of Dom Pérignon were made in tiny quantities compared with today and have aged into something closer to old white Burgundy. The 1985 Rosé is one of the house’s rarest bottlings.

wines.name: Jacques Selosse
wines.story: Anselme Selosse brought Burgundian thinking to Champagne: oak, oxidative ageing and a solera for the reserve wines. Initial is the entry point, the Rosé is one of the hardest bottles in the region to find.

wines.name: Louis Roederer Cristal
wines.story: Created in 1876 for Tsar Alexander II, who wanted a clear bottle with a flat bottom so nothing could be hidden inside it. The 1964 and 1966 are among the finest old Champagnes still drinking.

wines.name: Louis Roederer Rosé
wines.story: The first rosé vintage the house ever released. One bottle, more than half a century old, from a cellar that kept it in the dark.

holdings.condition: Super Rare! The first vintage ever produced***

wines.name: Salon ‘S’ Le Mesnil
wines.story: One village, one grape, one vintage, and only in years the house considers worthy: fewer than forty releases since 1905. Salon is released after a decade on its lees and rewards another.

wines.name: Egon Müller Scharzhofberger Auslese
wines.story: The Auslese is the wine Egon Müller is most often judged by: gold, weightless and capable of fifty years. From the same steep slate slope as the TBA.

wines.name: Egon Müller Scharzhofberger TBA
wines.story: Trockenbeerenauslese from the Scharzhofberg, picked berry by berry from shrivelled botrytised grapes, and made in a few hundred half bottles only in extraordinary years. The most expensive sweet wine in the world.

wines.name: Schloss Johannisberg Ex Bibliotheca Cuvée 100
wines.story: From the estate’s Bibliotheca, the cellar library where a few bottles of every vintage since 1748 are kept. A thousand bottles were filled of this Spätlese cuvée.

wines.name: Tokaji Essencia, Royal Tokaji
wines.story: The free-run juice of botrytised aszú berries, so rich in sugar that it takes years to ferment to a few degrees of alcohol. Served by the spoon, and reputed to raise the dying.

wines.name: Barbaresco Crichet Pajé, Roagna
wines.story: A single steep parcel of old vines, fermented for months on the skins and released after a decade in cask. Roagna bottles it only in the best years and in very small numbers.

wines.name: Barolo Monfortino Riserva, G. Conterno
wines.story: Made only in the finest years, from the Cascina Francia vineyard, and aged for seven years or more in large old casks. The 1978 is the vintage every Barolo drinker wants to have tasted once.

wines.name: Brunello Case Basse, Soldera
wines.story: Gianfranco Soldera made Sangiovese with the stubbornness of a saint, left the consorzio, and lost six vintages to a vandal who opened his casks in 2012. What survives from before is scarce and extraordinary.

wines.name: Masseto
wines.story: Seven hectares of blue clay on a hill above Ornellaia, planted to Merlot in 1984 almost by accident. It became Italy’s answer to Pétrus, and the only Italian wine traded like a first growth.

wines.name: Montepulciano d’Abruzzo, Emidio Pepe
wines.story: Grapes crushed by foot, wines aged in glass-lined cement and decanted by hand, bottle by bottle, before release. Emidio Pepe’s 1970s wines are among the greatest old Italian reds in existence.

wines.name: Ornellaia
wines.story: The first vintage commercially released, made by Lodovico Antinori on the estate his family had used for hunting. Four bottles from the year the Bolgheri legend began.

wines.name: Ribolla Gialla, Gravner & Radikon
wines.story: Two neighbours who reinvented white wine by fermenting it on the skins, Gravner in buried Georgian amphorae. Amber, tannic, and unlike anything else in the world.

holdings.condition: Sauvignon Blanc, Pinot Grigio, Chardonnay & Riesling

wines.name: Sassicaia
wines.story: Mario Incisa della Rocchetta planted Cabernet at Tenuta San Guido in the 1940s for his own table, and the 1968 was the first vintage sold. The 1985 remains the greatest Italian wine of its era, with a perfect score.

wines.name: Château Musar
wines.story: Serge Hochar made wine through the civil war, trucking grapes across front lines, and released each vintage seven years later. The 1970s Musars are among the great old reds of the Mediterranean.

wines.name: D’Oliveiras Madeira Sercial
wines.story: Madeira is the only wine that improves for two centuries and survives an open bottle for a year. D’Oliveiras keeps its oldest casks in Funchal and bottles on demand.

wines.name: Quinta do Noval Nacional
wines.story: Two and a half hectares of ungrafted vines in the middle of the Noval estate, which survived phylloxera and still produce a few hundred cases in declared years. The most mythical name in Port.

wines.name: Warre Vintage Port
wines.story: The oldest British Port house, founded in 1670. The 1947 is one of the great post-war declarations and is now at its peak.

wines.name: Château Rayas
wines.story: Pale, perfumed Grenache from cool sandy soils under pine trees, the opposite of what the appellation is supposed to taste like. Emmanuel Reynaud makes it as his uncle did, and the world waits.

wines.name: Château Rayas Blanc
wines.story: A few hundred cases of white from the same sandy vineyards, waxy and honeyed with age. Harder to find than the red, and adored by the sommeliers who know it.

wines.name: Cuvée des Célestins, Henri Bonneau
wines.story: Henri Bonneau made wine in a damp cellar under the village, in old barrels he refused to replace, and released it when he felt like it. The Célestins is Grenache from the pebbles of La Crau at its most profound.

wines.name: Ermitage Cuvée Cathelin, J-L Chave
wines.story: Made only in years Jean-Louis Chave judges exceptional, from the best barrels of the hill, and named after the painter Bernard Cathelin. Around two hundred cases each time, and every vintage offered here scores a perfect hundred.

wines.name: Hermitage La Chapelle, Jaboulet
wines.story: Named for the small chapel on top of the hill of Hermitage. The 1978 is the most famous wine Jaboulet ever made, and one of a handful of Rhônes to earn a perfect score from Robert Parker.

wines.name: Saint-Joseph Vieilles Vignes, Pierre Gonon
wines.story: The Gonon brothers farm the steep granite terraces of Mauves by hand. The old-vine bottling is a few barrels from vines planted before the war, released only in some years and almost never seen.

wines.name: Rivesaltes, Château Mossé
wines.story: Fortified Grenache aged for decades in cask and demijohn under the Roussillon sun. The 1931 has the colour of old mahogany and tastes of walnuts and orange peel.

wines.name: Château d’Yquem
wines.story: The only premier cru supérieur of the 1855 classification, made from botrytised grapes picked berry by berry. Yquem lives for a century or more; the 1894 was bottled when the château still belonged to the Lur-Saluces family.

wines.name: Château d’Yquem, halves
wines.story: The half bottle is the format Yquem was meant for at table: one glass each for six, with the last of the cheese. The 1990 is one of the estate’s three perfect vintages of the decade.

wines.name: Marsala Riserva ‘Bronte’, Woodhouse & Co.
wines.story: John Woodhouse, an English merchant, created the Marsala trade in 1773 and supplied Nelson’s fleet. This reserve was laid down in the year of Waterloo, in the barrels named for the Duchy of Bronte given to Nelson. The oldest liquid on the list.

wines.name: Comando G, Rumbo al Norte
wines.story: Half a hectare of old Garnacha on granite at 1,200 metres, farmed by two friends who made Gredos famous. Pale, perfumed and Burgundian; most vintages score a perfect hundred.

holdings.condition: the last vintage to be produced*

wines.name: La Faraona, Descendientes de J. Palacios
wines.story: A single terrace of half a hectare on quartz and slate, worked by mule by Ricardo Pérez Palacios. Around six hundred bottles a year and, in 2014, a perfect score.

wines.name: Las Beatas, Telmo Rodríguez
wines.story: Two hectares of abandoned terraces recovered stone by stone by Telmo Rodríguez, the man who rebuilt the reputation of old Spain. Both vintages here earned a perfect score.

wines.name: Pingus
wines.story: Peter Sisseck’s four hectares of very old vines, farmed biodynamically. A few hundred cases a year and, since the first vintage in 1995, Spain’s most sought-after modern wine.

wines.name: Vega Sicilia Único
wines.origin: Valbuena de Duero, Ribera del Duero
wines.story: Spain’s first great wine, released only after ten years in cask and bottle. The 1962 and 1968 are perfect-score vintages; the 1965 is described in the cellar book with one word: immaculate.

wines.name: Viña Tondonia, López de Heredia
wines.story: A bodega that has changed almost nothing since 1877: American oak, long ageing, cobwebs. The 1973 red and the 1976 white Reserva are what old Rioja is supposed to taste like.
